assessments.reasoning: Authenticity follows from spdx_detail in spdx/license-list-data at 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. Integrity follows from matching reported digests at [16343,16366), [16293,16340), [4,35) and [16636,16718). Relevance follows from those ranges recording the ID, name, deprecation flag and seeAlso respectively. Interpretation yields CC0-1.0, Creative Commons Zero v1.0 Universal, false for ID deprecation, and the publisher's legal-code URL. Applicability follows from spdx_data_tag.object.sha matching the JSON pin. On contradiction, JSON crossRef.url agrees with seeAlso and with spdx_xml [99,337). The deprecation field describes the SPDX identifier only.

Authenticity follows from publisher_readme at the same Creative Commons commit as publisher_pin. Integrity follows from its matching range digest at [4999,5294). Relevance follows from the publisher's own edition and canonical URL fields there. Interpretation identifies CC0 1.0 Universal, unit zero, version 1.0 and language en. Applicability follows because spdx_detail.seeAlso appends legalcode to that canonical URL and publisher_live supplies legalcode.txt under the same base. On contradiction, publisher_pin [0,48) names the same legal instrument, and its waiver distinguishes it from the Public Domain Mark. This dependency supplies publisher identity context only.

Authenticity follows from spdx_xml in spdx/license-list-XML at b1dbeb5c8bca21af860a90e187f71d60b84a7a40. Integrity follows from the matching reported digest at [99,337). Relevance follows from the license element and crossRef in that range. Interpretation gives licenseId CC0-1.0, name Creative Commons Zero v1.0 Universal and crossRef https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/legalcode. Applicability follows from spdx_xml_tag.object.sha matching that XML pin. On contradiction, direct comparison with spdx_detail at its separate data pin finds the same ID, name and URL in the JSON fields. This supports source-record lineage within SPDX.

Integrity follows from the matching whole-response digest at [0,700) and the matching object identity in sha. Relevance follows from tag, object.type and object.sha. Interpretation reads v3.29.0 with a direct commit target of 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. Applicability follows from that full target matching the inspected spdx_detail URL. On contradiction, spdx_generation.sha and its 3.29.0 build message agree. The verification field identifies an unsigned object, limiting authentication to repository attribution.

Authenticity follows from spdx_xml_tag at the spdx/license-list-XML Git tag-object endpoint for 7523cc3daa7149e35e2debd7466c1dcb14a84e19. Integrity follows from the matching whole-response digest at [0,698) and matching sha. Relevance follows from tag, object.type and object.sha. Interpretation reads v3.29.0 with a direct commit target of b1dbeb5c8bca21af860a90e187f71d60b84a7a40. Applicability follows from that full target matching the inspected spdx_xml URL. On contradiction, spdx_data_tag records the same release name in the data repository with its own distinct target, resolving a possible repository mix-up. The XML tag's verification field records unsigned status.

Authenticity follows from spdx_generation at the spdx/license-list-data Git commit endpoint for 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. Integrity follows from the matching whole-response digest at [0,1237) and matching sha. Relevance follows from the commit's message field. Interpretation of “License list build 3.29.0 using license list publisher 3.1.4” assigns each version to its stated role. Applicability follows because this commit is both the spdx_detail pin and the direct target of spdx_data_tag. On contradiction, the two tag names agree with the build version and the XML and JSON fields agree. The message supplies generated-data attribution without specifying an XML input SHA.

challenge.method: Compared XML licenseId, name and crossRef directly against JSON licenseId, name, crossRef.url and seeAlso. Compared both annotated tag targets with the respective file URL pins, then read the target data commit's own message. Checked the publisher edition separately to test a same-name, wrong-tool or summary-page match.
challenge.results: The three documentary values agree across the two revisions, and the reference ends in legalcode under the publisher's CC0 1.0 namespace. The tags have the same release name and different, repository-correct commit targets. The build message distinguishes the list version 3.29.0 from the generator version 3.1.4.

limitations: This is a documentary crosswalk for the inspected release. It establishes neither representation equivalence nor a copyright classification or grant for any project.
The XML, generated detail, tags and build record share SPDX information lineage. The tag and commit objects are unsigned.

The build message names the release and generator version but omits the XML input commit. The paired tags and matching fields support release-level lineage. Exact build inputs and reproducibility remain unverified.
reasoning: The pinned generated JSON records CC0-1.0, the name “Creative Commons Zero v1.0 Universal”, and a reference to the publisher's /publicdomain/zero/1.0/legalcode. The separately pinned XML agrees on all three values. Each repository's annotated v3.29.0 tag targets the exact commit inspected there. The generated-data commit message identifies the 3.29.0 build and publisher version 3.1.4. Creative Commons' own edition record and plaintext identify the instrument at the referenced publisher path.
